note: Considered-and-rejected candidates. Approval statuses are from live ChEMBL max_phase queries run 2026-10-12; literature claims carry resolved PMIDs (abstracts read via efetch). 'Rejected' here means rejected as a candidate for the MVA repurposing hypothesis - several remain legitimate drugs for their labeled indications.

entries.approval_status: approved (ChEMBL max_phase 4 class) - approval not the issue
entries.reason: Tempting target for the child's short stature/failure-to-thrive phenotype, but it treats a symptom while stimulating proliferation in a cancer-predisposition syndrome. In the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study, GH-treated survivors had a second-neoplasm rate ratio of 2.15 (95% CI 1.3-3.5) versus untreated survivors - an elevated SN signal in a population already cancer-prone, directly analogous to MVA risk biology. IGF-1-driven growth promotion in a child whose mosaic aneuploid clones are under relaxed surveillance is the wrong direction.
entries.note: Re-evaluate only if endocrine workup shows true GH deficiency and oncology signs off; not a repurposing candidate here.

entries.approval_status: ChEMBL443684 max_phase 3, no first_approval recorded (live query 2026-10-12)
entries.reason: Potent BCL-2/BCL-xL senolytic - mechanistically the most direct senolytic after D+Q - but fails the hard rule: market-approved medications only. Additionally causes dose-limiting thrombocytopenia (BCL-xL in platelets), undesirable in a child.
entries.note: If a BCL-xL/BCL-2 senolytic gains approval, re-screen; dasatinib covers the senolytic axis today.

entries.reason: Not a market-approved drug. Retained only as the adjunct half of the D+Q senolytic pair whose human pilot data exist (PMID:31542391); it cannot anchor a candidate on its own under the approved-only rule.
Flavonoid senolytic in trials, but not a market-approved medication; excluded by the approved-only rule. Could appear in the MVA Society supplements program outside the drug dossier set.

entries.approval_status: NR: CHEMBL438497 max_phase 3, no approval; NMN: no approved entry (live queries 2026-10-12)
entries.reason: NMN is literally the NAD+ precursor that raised BubR1 abundance in the anchor study (PMID:24825348) - mechanistically the most direct Axis-A agent - but neither form is a market-approved drug. Approved NAD precursors (niacin, niacinamide) carry the dossier instead; NR/NMN remain adjuncts fitting the MVA Society supplements program.
Co-headliner of the tetraploid-elimination screen (with aspirin) but a supplement, not a medication; also has poor bioavailability. Aspirin carries the dossier for this mechanism.

entries.drug: MPS1 (TTK) inhibitors (e.g. reversine-class), Aurora kinase inhibitors, KIF18A inhibitors
entries.approval_status: investigational oncology agents; none approved for this purpose
entries.reason: These drugs exist to weaken or exploit the spindle assembly checkpoint and spindle mechanics in cancer. Aneuploid cancer cells are indeed selectively vulnerable to SAC/KIF18A perturbation (Nature 2021: synthetic-lethal aneuploidy-SAC interaction) - but that is a tumour-killing strategy. In an MVA child the residual SAC in NORMAL mosaic cells is what limits new aneuploidy; systemic SAC inhibition would accelerate mis-segregation in every dividing tissue - pharmacologically recreating the disease mechanism. Rejected for preventive/chronic use; the vulnerability may matter later only if a frank malignancy is being treated by oncologists.

entries.drug: p53-pathway inhibition (e.g. pifithrin-class; no approved selective agent)
entries.approval_status: no approved selective p53 inhibitor exists
entries.reason: Proposed by naive reasoning as 'relieve the growth arrest' for failure-to-thrive, but p53 is the brake that limits proliferation of aneuploid cells; disabling it removes the main tumour-suppressive barrier in a syndrome whose cancers emerge from aneuploid clones. Direction is pro-oncogenic - the opposite of the goal.

entries.drug: antimitotic agents (taxanes, vinca alkaloids, benzimidazole anthelmintics incl. mebendazole)
entries.approval_status: approved for oncology/anthelmintic indications, not for this purpose
entries.reason: Spindle-poisons cause chromosome mis-segregation - the exact lesion MVA already produces. Benzimidazoles specifically show aneugenic activity in micronucleus assays. Mebendazole surfaced in the systematic screen (aneuploid-selective killing query) but is rejected on this mechanism.

entries.approval_status: tanespimycin CHEMBL109480 max_phase 3, no approval (live query 2026-10-12); no HSP90 inhibitor is approved
entries.reason: 17-AAG was one of the three aneuploidy-selective compounds in the founding screen (proteotoxic-stress angle) - but the class never reached approval (development abandoned on toxicity/efficacy), and chaperone inhibition destabilises client kinases broadly. Excluded on the approved-only rule; the selectivity rationale is covered by chloroquine in the HCQ dossier.

The energy-stress hit in the aneuploidy-selective screen (p53-dependent apoptosis in trisomic MEFs) - mechanistically appealing, but not market-approved. Metformin is the nearest approved energy-stress/AMPK agent and carries the analogy in its dossier.

entries.approval_status: research compounds only (TAME characterised as an APC/C inhibitor, Nat Chem Biol 2012)
entries.reason: BubR1 restrains APC/C; an APC/C inhibitor sits downstream of the defect and would mimic/amplify checkpoint failure rather than rescue it. Also not approved.

entries.approval_status: no approved SIRT2 activator exists; selective SIRT2 tool compounds are investigational
entries.reason: Pharmacologically the cleanest Axis-A lever (stabilise BubR1 via K668 deacetylation) but no approved agent exists; the feasible proxy is NAD+ repletion (niacin/nicotinamide dossier). Selective SIRT2 INHIBITORS exist but point the wrong way for this disease.
Surfaced in the systematic screen. In yeast mutation-accumulation lines it elevated mutation rates broadly with a particularly high occurrence of aneuploidy - the precise phenotype to avoid in MVA.

Considered because it could replace a compartment that accumulates aneuploid clones (e.g. marrow). The only published MVA1 HSCT case (11-year-old, MDS with monosomy 7): TCRab/CD19-depleted RIC transplant engrafted but was followed by day +47 graft rejection, prolonged pancytopenia and fatal sepsis (death day +156). Does not address aneuploidy in non-hematopoietic tissues; single-case evidence is adverse.

entries.approval_status: transgenic research system, not a medication
entries.reason: This is the actual intervention that rescued the BubR1-hypomorph mouse phenotype in Nature 2011 - the scientific anchor for the whole Axis-B hypothesis - listed here explicitly so the record is honest that the anchor intervention is a gene circuit, not a drug. Dasatinib+quercetin is its pharmacologic approximation.
